note: All numbers are from pinned-fork simulations (Foundry, latest block 2026-10-21) executed in CI. Oracle threshold: gOHM 3,119.289 USDS/gOHM = OHM $11.586 (index 269.238508004). ETH $2,515.71, sUSDS PPS 1.11360497.

sell_side_ohm_to_susds_0p3.note: pool drained to min tick; no more bid

full_crash_cost_both_venues.result: marginal OHM $11.0 (gOHM ~2,962, i.e. <= oracle threshold); attacker holds ZERO cheap gOHM (sold all inventory)
full_crash_cost_both_venues.conclusion: cost to crash the spot to the oracle threshold is ~$331k, but it is a pure loss: the only counterparty to the dump is the AMM the attacker must buy back from

same_pool_round_trip_self.conclusion: sell-then-buy round trip returns the SAME 40,000 OHM and loses ~2x pool fees (0.3%+0.3%=0.6%) plus tick rounding. Confirms: manipulation cannot change the attacker's own gOHM holdings.

buy_side_depth_below_oracle_gifted_panic.note: Model: a THIRD PARTY crashes the OHM/WETH pool to the target, then the attacker buys OHM (==gOHM) until the marginal price returns to the oracle threshold. This is the maximum acquirable below the oracle IF the crash is free. The attacker cannot cause the crash (see round_trip / full_crash_cost).
buy_side_depth_below_oracle_gifted_panic.ceiling: bounded by the DEX bid depth (~$0.93M in the deep pool; ~$1.8M across all OHM venues). Even a crash to OHM $2 only frees ~582 gOHM / ~$0.89M of profit on the deep venue. Adding the sUSDS pool (~$0.87M bid) roughly doubles it to ~$1.7M — still far below the $1.39M-$3.6M treasury headroom, and it requires a GIFTED panic.

self_crash_then_buy.conclusion: a self-funded crash yields only ~16 gOHM before the marginal returns to the oracle; net loss. The $197k of crash impact is unrecoverable.
